SP-HLM: Sparse-Pose-Driven Motion Generation and Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation HumanoidEmbodied

sparse-pose interface vision-language-action (VLA) motion generation whole-body control loco-manipulation

简要说明：SP-HLM 提出了一种基于稀疏姿态驱动的接口，用于人形机器人移动操作，结合 VLA 模型用于稀疏姿态预测、运动生成模型和全身跟踪器，在仿真和真实硬件上展示了改进的协调性和成功率。

TLDR: SP-HLM introduces a sparse-pose-driven interface for humanoid loco-manipulation, combining a VLA model for sparse pose prediction with a motion generation model and a whole-body tracker, demonstrating improved coordination and success in simulation and on real hardware.

Abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires an effective interface between high-level task policies and whole-body control. Existing interfaces typically rely on a single action representation for both task intent and whole-body coordination. This may burden the high-level policy or leave one aspect underspecified. We present SP-HLM, a framework built on a sparse-pose-driven interface. The interface combines five task-critical body poses with a learned latent motion prior to represent spatial intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms. SP-VLA, a vision-language-action model, first predicts task-relevant sparse poses and finger joint positions from multimodal observations and language instructions using asynchronous action-chunk inference. Given these sparse targets, SP-MGM, a motion generation model trained through two-stage distillation, reconstructs coordinated full-body motion in real time. A pretrained motion encoder maps this motion to a compact latent representation. SP-GMT, a general motion tracker, then integrates the explicit sparse targets with this implicit motion prior for whole-body control. Experiments in simulation and on a real humanoid robot demonstrate improved motion tracking, whole-body coordination, and loco-manipulation success over existing approaches. Additional results and videos are available on our \href{https://sp-hlm.github.io/}{\textcolor{blue}{project page}}.

摘要（中文）：人形机器人全身操控需要在高层次任务策略与全身控制之间建立有效的接口。现有接口通常依赖单一的动作表示来同时承载任务意图与全身协调，这可能导致高层次策略负担过重，或使某一方面的信息表达不足。我们提出SP-HLM，一个基于稀疏姿态驱动接口的框架。该接口结合五种任务关键身体姿态与学习得到的潜空间运动先验，以互补形式分别表达空间意图与全身协调。SP-VLA作为一种视觉-语言-动作模型，首先利用异步动作块推理，从多模态观测与语言指令中预测与任务相关的稀疏姿态及手指关节位置。在获得这些稀疏目标后，SP-MGM通过两阶段蒸馏训练的运动生成模型，实时重建协调的全身运动。预训练的运动编码器将该运动映射为紧凑的潜空间表示。SP-GMT作为通用运动跟踪器，将显式稀疏目标与该隐式运动先验相融合，用于全身控制。在仿真环境与真实人形机器人上的实验表明，与现有方法相比，本框架在运动跟踪、全身协调以及全身操控成功率方面均有显著提升。更多结果与视频请参见我们的项目主页。

Authors: Zhaohui Yang, Quanbao Lin, Chengqi Shi, Zhenglang Weng, Jicheng Lin, Boyu Chen, Tengjie Zhu, Guanzhu Ren, Jiahao Xu, Yang Feng, Xiaokang Yang, Yao Mu

FlowVLA: Learning Flow-Aware Physical Completion for Quantitative Robotic Pouring VLA

Vision-Language-Action Physical Completion Force Belief Robotic Pouring Generalization

简要说明：FlowVLA 提出了一种流量感知的 VLA 策略，将电机生成与物理完成度估计分离，利用力信念历史与残余流出预测实现精准机器人倒水，并泛化至未见过目标量。

TLDR: FlowVLA introduces a flow-aware VLA policy that separates motor generation from physical-completion estimation, using force-belief histories and residual-outflow prediction to achieve accurate robotic pouring with held-out target generalization.

Abstract: During steady pouring, images and robot pose may remain nearly unchanged while transferred mass accumulates, making the return decision ambiguous for a whole-task vision-language-action (VLA) policy. We present FlowVLA, which separates motor generation from physical-completion estimation. A shared $π_{0.5}$ action expert learns approach, pour, and return with boundary-aware supervision. A target-independent estimator fuses visual, joint, wrist-wrench, and recurrent force-belief histories to maintain an estimate of transferred mass. The controller initiates return when this estimate plus predicted residual outflow reaches the requested mass. In coffee-pot/water experiments, FlowVLA achieves 13.1 g goal-balanced mean absolute error (MacroMAE), lower than all tested VLA baselines. Across all attempts, 53.7% both complete the task and finish within +/-10% of the requested mass. The same model interpolates to held-out 150/250-g targets without retraining. Independently trained models further evaluate the formulation in three additional container-fluid settings.

摘要（中文）：在持续浇注过程中，图像与机器人位姿可能几乎保持不变，而转移质量却在不断累积，这使得面向整体任务的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略在判断何时返回时面临模糊性。我们提出了FlowVLA，将电机生成与物理完成度估计分离。一个共享的π₀.₅动作专家在边界感知监督下学习接近、浇注和返回动作。一个与目标无关的估计器融合视觉、关节、腕部力矩及循环力信念历史，持续估计已转移质量。当该估计值加上预测的残余流出量达到目标质量时，控制器即触发返回动作。在咖啡壶/水实验中，FlowVLA实现了13.1克的目标均衡平均绝对误差（MacroMAE），低于所有测试的VLA基线模型。在所有尝试中，53.7%的试验既完成了任务，又将最终质量控制在请求质量的±10%以内。同一模型无需重新训练即可泛化至未参与训练的150/250克目标。独立训练的模型进一步在另外三种容器-流体场景中评估了该方法的有效性。

Authors: Liwen Yang, Yutian Zhang, Jiaqi Zhai, Li Yang, Tutian Tang, Qiwei Shan, Yancheng Bi, Qiankuan Shangguan, Yangkun Zhu, Ce Hao, Dong Wei, Qiaojun Yu, Dibo Hou

SimPT: An Automated Simulation Framework for Intervention-Based VLA Post-Training VLA

VLA post-training simulation framework expert recovery progress graph robot manipulation

简要说明：SimPT 通过代理编译进度图自动检测失败并调度 CuRobo 恢复，在仿真中自动化干预式 VLA 后训练，提升了真实机器人任务成功率。

TLDR: SimPT automates intervention-based VLA post-training in simulation using an Agent-Compiled Progress Graph to detect failures and schedule CuRobo recovery, enabling algorithmic exploration and improving real-robot success rates.

Abstract: Human-in-the-loop (HIL) post-training improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies through expert corrections, but costly human supervision and repeated real-robot evaluation limit algorithm exploration and development. We introduce SimPT (Simulation-based Post-Training), a simulation framework that automates intervention-based VLA post-training by integrating policy rollouts, corrective data collection, policy training, and standalone evaluation. To automatically determine intervention timing and recovery strategies, we develop an Agent-Compiled Progress Graph that tracks task progress using privileged simulator state and retains stable snapshots during policy execution. After a rollout fails, a CuRobo-based expert attempts recovery from these snapshots, starting at more advanced task stages and falling back to earlier ones as needed to generate corrective trajectories. We implement and compare four post-training methods, RECAP, HG-DAgger, DPO+SFT, and FlowPRO, across seven RoboTwin manipulation tasks. Relative to a fixed-interval snapshot baseline, the Progress Graph reduces recovery attempts by 75.0% and increases recovery success from 93.4% to 98.9%. Using SimPT, we develop RECAP-CF-LPF, a refinement of RECAP that combines cross-fitting and low-pass filtering of value predictions. This refinement increases the overall success rate from 76.50% to 79.36% in held-out simulation trials. In real-robot HIL post-training, it increases the success rate from 72% to 96% across 25 scenarios of an Ethernet cable-insertion task. These results demonstrate the utility of SimPT for exploring and developing VLA post-training algorithms.

摘要（中文）：人在回路（HIL）后训练通过专家修正提升视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略，但高昂的人工监督成本和反复的真实机器人评估限制了算法的探索与开发。本文提出SimPT（基于仿真的后训练），一种仿真框架，通过整合策略 rollout、修正数据采集、策略训练和独立评估，实现基于干预的VLA后训练自动化。为自动确定干预时机和恢复策略，我们开发了一种代理编译进度图，该图利用特权仿真器状态追踪任务进度，并在策略执行过程中保留稳定快照。当一次 rollout 失败后，基于 CuRobo 的专家尝试从这些快照开始恢复，优先从更高级的任务阶段出发，必要时回退到较早阶段，以生成修正轨迹。我们在七个 RoboTwin 操作任务上实现并比较了四种后训练方法：RECAP、HG-DAgger、DPO+SFT 和 FlowPRO。与固定间隔快照基线相比，进度图将恢复尝试次数减少了75.0%，并将恢复成功率从93.4%提升至98.9%。利用SimPT，我们开发了RECAP-CF-LPF，这是对RECAP的改进，结合了交叉拟合和值预测的低通滤波。该改进在保留仿真试验中将总体成功率从76.50%提升至79.36%。在真实机器人HIL后训练中，在以太网电缆插入任务的25个场景中，成功率从72%提升至96%。这些结果证明了SimPT在探索和开发VLA后训练算法方面的实用性。

Authors: Caicheng Wang, Zipeng Ye, Zhexuan Zhou, Zilong Huang, Xi Zhang, Yuchen Xie

Real2Sem2Real: 3D Semantic Augmentations for Robot Learning from a Single Human RGB Demonstration VLA

DINOv3-distilled Gaussian splats semantic alignment digital cousins sim-to-real vision-language-action policy

简要说明：R2Sem2R 将单个单目RGB人类演示视频转化为数千个机器人演示，通过语义对齐和仿真到现实迁移，训练出的VLA策略在多种物体上达到或超过遥操作性能。

TLDR: R2Sem2R converts a single monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations via semantic alignment of digital cousins and sim-to-real transfer, enabling VLA policy training that matches teleoperation performance across diverse objects.

Abstract: Human video scales easily and does not need robot hardware, but existing methods require depth sensing, overlay the robot onto 2D video, or generate data only for the demonstrated objects. We present Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R), a real-to-semantic-to-real pipeline that turns one monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations across the semantic object instances of a category. R2Sem2R tracks the SE(3) pose of each object with DINOv3-distilled Gaussian splats, outperforming existing methods and FoundationPose with estimated metric depth. R2Sem2R then aligns digital cousins, each generated from one or a few photographs, to the demonstrated objects with a semantic alignment. This alignment matches whole objects and the functional regions of target objects, such as a coffee machine's tray. R2Sem2R maps the human hand to a feasible robot grasp that extends to the cousins. Robot demonstrations are generated either in IsaacSim, for photorealistic rendering, or MuJoCo, for contact physics, and R2Sem2R can generate over 2,000 episodes in about two hours. On two real robots and four tasks, we train a vision-language-action policy on data from one human video per task, and policies trained on our data match or exceed policies trained on teleoperation across diverse object instances. The project page is available at https://real2sem2real.github.io/.

摘要（中文）：人类视频易于获取且无需机器人硬件，但现有方法需要深度感知、将机器人叠加到二维视频上，或仅为已演示的物体生成数据。我们提出Real2Sem2Real（R2Sem2R）——一种从真实到语义再回到真实的处理流程，可将人类演示的单目RGB视频转化为跨类别语义物体实例的数千条机器人演示。R2Sem2R利用DINOv3蒸馏的高斯溅射跟踪每个物体的SE(3)位姿，在估计度量深度下优于现有方法和FoundationPose。随后，R2Sem2R将通过一张或数张照片生成的数字孪生体与演示物体进行语义对齐，该对齐匹配整体物体及其功能区域，例如咖啡机托盘。R2Sem2R将人类手部映射为可行的机器人抓取，并推广至孪生体。机器人演示可在IsaacSim（用于照片级真实感渲染）或MuJoCo（用于接触物理）中生成，R2Sem2R可在约两小时内生成超过2,000条演示。在两个真实机器人和四个任务上，我们利用每个任务的单条人类视频数据训练视觉-语言-动作策略，基于我们数据训练的策略在多样化物体实例上达到或超过基于遥操作训练的策略。项目页面见https://real2sem2real.github.io/。

Authors: Matthew Strong, Ankush K. Dhawan, Julien Poffet, Giuse Pham, Jinho So, Monroe Kennedy

GeoMem-VLA: Internalizing 3D Scene Understanding into Temporal Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models VLA

Vision-Language-Action models 3D scene understanding Temporal memory Geometric tokens Robotic manipulation

简要说明：GeoMem-VLA 提出了一种 VLA 框架，将 3D 场景理解内化为可学习的几何标记并作为时间记忆维护，在 LIBERO、RoboTwin 和真实世界操作任务上取得了优异性能，且推理时无需 3D 监督。

TLDR: GeoMem-VLA introduces a VLA framework that internalizes 3D scene understanding into learnable geometric tokens maintained as temporal memory, achieving strong performance on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and real-world manipulation tasks without requiring 3D supervision at inference.

Abstract: Geometric structure is essential for robotic manipulation and understanding the 3D world. Most VLA models rely on 2D representations of current observations, while geometry-aware approaches often require additional 3D information. However, geometry inferred independently from individual observations is often discarded rather than accumulated into a persistent task representation. Our key insight is that action generation needs a compact, task-relevant geometric abstraction that can be continuously updated, rather than a complete, renderable 3D reconstruction at every step. We introduce GeoMem-VLA, a VLA framework that internalizes explicit 3D supervision into dedicated geometric tokens and maintains them as temporal memory for action generation, without directly aligning the VLM's native visual embeddings with the teacher feature space. During training, a frozen geometry foundation model supervises learnable GeoPlan tokens through a geometric flow-matching objective over the current scene point map and future end-effector tracks. These tokens are integrated with the memory of observation representations, where historical information is retrieved, adaptively fused with current observations, and consolidated to retain event frames as the task progresses. At inference, the policy retrieves historical representations and fuses them with the current working representation to predict actions, without invoking the 3D teacher or explicitly reconstructing the scene. After benchmark-specific downstream adaptation, GeoMem-VLA achieves 98.9% average success on LIBERO and 91.10% / 91.24% on RoboTwin's clean/randomized settings. Across five real-world tasks, GeoMem-VLA achieves 78.0% average success. These results suggest that internalizing and remembering 3D scene understanding is a promising approach to robot control.

摘要（中文）：几何结构对于机器人操作和理解三维世界至关重要。大多数VLA模型依赖于当前观测的二维表示，而几何感知方法通常需要额外的三维信息。然而，从单次观测中独立推断出的几何信息往往被丢弃，而非累积为持久的任务表示。我们的关键见解是：动作生成需要的是一种紧凑的、与任务相关的几何抽象，且能够持续更新，而非在每一步都进行完整的、可渲染的三维重建。我们提出GeoMem-VLA，这是一种VLA框架，将显式的三维监督内化为专用的几何令牌，并将其作为时序记忆用于动作生成，而无需将VLM的原生视觉嵌入与教师特征空间直接对齐。在训练阶段，冻结的几何基础模型通过几何流匹配目标对可学习的GeoPlan令牌进行监督，该目标基于当前场景点图和未来末端执行器轨迹。这些令牌与观测表示的记忆相整合，其中历史信息被检索、与当前观测自适应融合，并在任务推进过程中整合以保留事件帧。在推理阶段，策略检索历史表示并将其与当前工作表示融合以预测动作，而无需调用三维教师模型或显式重建场景。经过基准特定的下游适配后，GeoMem-VLA在LIBERO上达到98.9%的平均成功率，在RoboTwin的干净/随机设置上分别达到91.10%和91.24%。在五个真实世界任务中，GeoMem-VLA达到78.0%的平均成功率。这些结果表明，将三维场景理解内化并记忆是机器人控制的一种有前景的方法。

Authors: Qinfan Zhang, Yifan Luo, Haoyuan Shi, Guanlin Liu, Han Dong, Haozhe Shan, Yong Dai, Xiangcong Ren, Xiaozhu Ju

Agentic World Action Models Manipulation

Agentic World Action Model Code-based planning Video and action prediction Mixture-of-transformers Skill libraries

简要说明：本文提出 AW-0，一种智能体世界动作模型，在统一的混合Transformer架构中整合基于代码的规划与视频和动作预测，相较于现有VLA和WAM基线，提升了操作任务性能和鲁棒性。

TLDR: The paper proposes AW-0, an agentic world action model that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction in a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture, improving manipulation task performance and robustness over existing VLA and WAM baselines.

Abstract: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. Evaluations on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual manipulation tasks show improved task performance over VLA and WAM baselines, alongside gains in language following, semantic reasoning and robustness, demonstrating that agentic code enables connection between planning, prediction and execution within WAMs.

摘要（中文）：近期推出的世界动作模型为机器人操作提供了视觉预判与未来预测能力，但缺乏组合性技能复用的显式机制。智能体机器人技术将基于代码的规划与推理同可复用技能相结合，却往往缺少对物理动力学的预测性锚定。为此，我们提出AW-0，一种智能体世界动作模型框架，将基于代码的规划与联合视频及动作预测融为一体。我们在统一的混合变换器架构中，将代码、未来视频及机器人动作共同建模为三条耦合的生成流。在该架构中，代码专家负责生成参数化技能例程与控制逻辑，而视频与动作专家则分别生成未来视觉状态和低级运动指令。代码在此扮演两个互补角色：一方面在世界模型内部构建多步预测与控制的框架，另一方面将技能表示为可复用的程序，以供后续智能体执行使用。我们还引入了一条自动化整理流程，为机器人与人类视频轨迹标注对应的程序，并将重复出现的例程整合为可复用的技能库。在RoboTwin 2.0及实体双臂操作任务上的评估显示，相较于VLA与WAM基线，任务表现得到提升，同时在语言指令跟随、语义推理及鲁棒性方面亦有增益，从而证明智能体代码能在世界动作模型内部打通规划、预测与执行之间的连接。

Authors: Zhuoyang Liu, Dantong Niu, Botong Zhang, Boning Shao, Jing Wang, Ruijie Zheng, Yuvan Sharma, Runyu Lu, Jiaming Liu, Renrui Zhang, Roei Herzig, Yutong Bai, Ken Goldberg, Danfei Xu, Yuke Zhu, Guanzhi Wang, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Trevor Darrell

CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation Manipulation

contact wrench world action model force-sensitive manipulation admittance control motion-wrench chunks

简要说明：CW-WAM提出了一种世界动作模型，联合预测视频、运动和接触力，利用配对因果注意力和力记忆，显著提高力敏感操作中的插入成功率和力精度。

TLDR: CW-WAM introduces a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench, using a pair-causal attention mechanism and wrench memory to improve force-sensitive manipulation, significantly increasing insertion success rates and force accuracy with an admittance controller.

Abstract: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predicted wrench chunk acts as a force reference for a 20-Hz outer-loop admittance controller within a slow-fast control system that maintains force feedback and smooth motion between model queries. CW-WAM improves contact prediction and increases the insertion success rate from 25% to 70% for square pegs with 1-mm clearance per side and from 40% to 95% for power adapters, compared with WAM without wrench input. It also improves lifting-height accuracy across different loads. Our framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE from 4.8 to 2.7 N for peg insertion and from 2.0 to 1.3 N for wiping, respectively, with smaller force fluctuations during successful execution. Project website: https://cw-wam-project.github.io/

摘要（中文）：力敏操作需要接触与载荷信息，而这些信息无法通过视觉观测直接获得。我们提出了CW-WAM，一种联合预测视频、运动与接触力旋量的世界动作模型。受混合运动-力控制启发，该模型包含一个统一交互模块，将运动与接触力旋量均作为建模目标，并预测时间对齐的运动-力旋量块作为控制参考。一种成对因果注意力机制构建了运动-力旋量之间的依赖关系，而一个长固定长度的力旋量记忆保留了过往交互信息。预测的力旋量块作为20赫兹外环导纳控制器的力参考，该系统采用慢-快控制架构，在模型查询之间维持力反馈与平滑运动。与无力旋量输入的WAM相比，CW-WAM在接触预测方面有所改进，并将边长1毫米间隙的方销插入成功率从25%提升至70%，电源适配器插入成功率从40%提升至95%。同时，在不同载荷下的抬升高度精度也得到提升。我们的框架结合导纳控制器，将销插入的力参考均方根误差从4.8牛降至2.7牛，擦拭任务从2.0牛降至1.3牛，且在成功执行过程中力波动更小。项目网站：https://cw-wam-project.github.io/

Authors: Houzhu Ding, Xinda Qi, Luqi Wang, Ming Yang

Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration Manipulation

on-policy distillation partial observability in-context exploration student-teacher learning real-world robot manipulation

简要说明：ASTEROID 是一种学生-教师蒸馏框架，通过在策略上下文上蒸馏特权专家动作来训练历史条件策略，在部分可观测环境下实现高效探索，并在多种环境和真实机器人操作中取得成效。

TLDR: ASTEROID is a student-teacher distillation framework that trains history-conditioned policies to explore under partial observability by distilling privileged expert actions on on-policy contexts, achieving efficient exploration across diverse environments and real-robot manipulation.

Abstract: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. Learning such information-gathering behaviors tabula rasa via online reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient, whereas offline imitation averages expert actions across hidden states and fails to learn exploration. In this work, we propose ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration. Although a privileged expert never needs to explore, we demonstrate that a history-conditioned student can learn to do so when trained with on-policy contexts: the student first collects on-policy context under partial observability, and the privileged expert provides action labels conditioned on that context. By distilling expert actions directly conditioned on the student's on-policy history, the student learns to systematically resolve partial observability, i.e., search while uncertain and exploit once the hidden state is revealed. This enables efficient test-time exploration (similar to Bayesian posterior sampling) without incurring the impractical training-data costs of reinforcement learning. Across a diverse range of eleven different environments, including discrete exploration benchmarks, robotic manipulation, navigation, and Procgen environments, ASTEROID achieves ~2x higher returns under fixed exploration budgets, uses ~100x fewer interactions than RL baselines, and outperforms frontier models at exploration. Finally, our method transfers policies trained in simulation to vision-denied real-world robot manipulation, exhibiting efficient exploration and increasing success by +40% over standard distillation. Overall, it provides a simple yet surprisingly effective framework to learn efficient test-time exploration.

摘要（中文）：部分可观测条件下的序贯决策具有较大难度，因为智能体必须通过探索来推断隐藏的、与任务相关的信息，之后才能有效行动。通过在线强化学习从零开始学习此类信息收集行为，样本效率较低；而离线模仿学习则会对隐藏状态下的专家动作进行平均，无法学习探索行为。在本工作中，我们提出ASTEROID，一种简单而有效的师生监督学习框架，能够学习测试时的探索行为。尽管特权专家永远不需要探索，我们证明了在策略内上下文条件下训练的历史条件学生模型可以学会探索：学生模型首先在部分可观测条件下收集策略内上下文，随后特权专家基于该上下文提供动作标签。通过直接基于学生模型的策略内历史来蒸馏专家动作，学生模型能够系统地解决部分可观测性问题，即在不确定时进行搜索，在隐藏状态被揭示后加以利用。这使得高效测试时探索（类似于贝叶斯后验采样）成为可能，同时避免了强化学习中不切实际的训练数据成本。在涵盖十一个不同环境的多样化测试中，包括离散探索基准、机器人操作、导航和Procgen环境，ASTEROID在固定探索预算下实现了约2倍更高的回报，交互次数比强化学习基线少约100倍，并在探索任务上优于前沿模型。最后，我们的方法可将仿真环境中训练的策略迁移到无视觉反馈的真实机器人操作中，展现出高效探索能力，且成功率比标准蒸馏方法提高40%。总体而言，本方法为学习高效测试时探索提供了一种简单但效果显著令人惊讶的框架。

Authors: Sriyash Poddar, Yanda Bao, Jacob Krantz, Matthew Chang, Xavier Puig, Roozbeh Mottaghi, Natasha Jaques, Abhishek Gupta

AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation VLA

reinforcement learning long-horizon manipulation VLA credit assignment sim2real

简要说明：AtomicRL是一个用于VLA策略的强化学习后训练框架，利用原子任务结构、语义感知门控和瓶颈自适应探索来提升长时程操作任务，并包含Real2Sim2Real部署流程。

TLDR: AtomicRL is an RL post-training framework for VLA policies that uses atomic task structures, semantic-aware gating, and bottleneck-adaptive exploration to improve long-horizon manipulation, with a Real2Sim2Real pipeline for deployment.

Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in robotic manipulation, but imitation learning (IL) alone often struggles to master complex long-horizon skills. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers an effective avenue for further improving VLA policies. However, existing VLA-RL methods typically suffer from delayed and biased credit assignment due to trajectory-level sparse rewards, while imbalanced subtask mastery creates bottlenecks that limit overall performance. To address these challenges, we propose AtomicRL, an RL post-training framework that leverages atomic task structures for reliable credit assignment and adaptive exploration. AtomicRL introduces Semantic-Aware Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses semantic-aware gating to constrain TD residuals from failed atomic subtasks from propagating across task boundaries, mitigating credit contamination while preserving intra-subtask credit assignment and value bootstrapping. In addition, Bottleneck-Adaptive Target Exploration (BATE) dynamically coordinates task sampling and local exploration incentives based on the mastery of individual atomic subtasks, directing learning toward the remaining bottlenecks. Finally, we develop a Real2Sim2Real pipeline that bridges online RL in simulation with real-world deployment, facilitating practical transfer to physical robots. On LIBERO-LONG, AtomicRL achieves absolute performance gains of 3.6% and 4.0% over PPO across two VLA architectures. On CALVIN ABC-D, it improves full-task performance by up to 9.5% over PPO. Combined with the Real2Sim2Real pipeline, AtomicRL further improves real-world task performance by an average of 21.3%. These results demonstrate that AtomicRL effectively improves the learning efficiency and manipulation performance of VLA policies on long-horizon tasks.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型在机器人操作中展现出巨大潜力，但仅依靠模仿学习（IL）往往难以掌握复杂的长时序技能。强化学习（RL）为进一步提升VLA策略提供了有效途径。然而，现有的VLA-RL方法通常因轨迹级稀疏奖励而产生延迟且偏置的信用分配问题，同时子任务掌握程度的不均衡形成了制约整体性能的瓶颈。为解决上述挑战，我们提出AtomicRL，一种利用原子任务结构实现可靠信用分配与自适应探索的RL后训练框架。AtomicRL引入语义感知策略优化（SAPO），利用语义感知门控约束失败原子子任务的TD残差跨任务边界传播，在缓解信用污染的同时保留子任务内部的信用分配与价值自举。此外，瓶颈自适应目标探索（BATE）根据各原子子任务的掌握程度动态协调任务采样与局部探索激励，将学习引导至剩余瓶颈。最后，我们开发了Real2Sim2Real流水线，将仿真中的在线RL与真实世界部署相衔接，促进向实体机器人的实际迁移。在LIBERO-LONG上，AtomicRL在两种VLA架构下相较于PPO分别取得3.6%和4.0%的绝对性能提升。在CALVIN ABC-D上，其将完整任务性能相对于PPO提升最高达9.5%。结合Real2Sim2Real流水线，AtomicRL进一步将真实世界任务性能平均提升21.3%。上述结果表明，AtomicRL有效提升了VLA策略在长时序任务中的学习效率与操作性能。

Authors: Likui Zhang, Zhe Zhu, Zhihao Zhan, Yibo Bai, Hanlin Wang, Dongwei Li, Bin Wang, Tianle Zhang, Xiaodan Liang, Liang Lin

Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer Locomotion

humanoid locomotion gravity transfer terrain geometry soil contact sim-to-sim

简要说明：本文研究了学习的人形机器人运动控制器从地球到月球条件下的迁移，改变了重力、地形几何和土壤接触模型，发现重力迁移不对称，且粗糙地形训练可提高鲁棒性。

TLDR: This paper studies the transfer of learned humanoid locomotion controllers from Earth to Moon conditions, varying gravity, terrain geometry, and soil contact models, and finds asymmetric gravity transfer and that rough terrain training improves robustness.

Abstract: The Moon changes gravity, terrain, and soil at once. Learned locomotion has studied reduced gravity on rigid ground and granular terrain mostly at Earth gravity, but not humanoids under both, generalist-controller transfer, or the Earth cost of lunar adaptation. On a simulated Unitree G1, we train 12 policies with one recipe, varying gravity, terrain geometry, and ground contact (rigid or three-dimensional resistive force theory, 3D RFT), and including Earth-to-Moon fine-tuning and gravity randomization. We test them at both gravities on rigid ground and 3D RFT, and at their training gravity on three held-out soil models. We also test the frozen SONIC, a released generalist humanoid controller, at both gravities on rigid ground only. Gravity transfer is asymmetric. Earth-trained policies keep 0.64 to 0.75 survival at the Moon on flat rigid ground, Moon-trained and fine-tuned policies cannot stand at Earth, and SONIC survives at most 0.10 at the Moon. Rough training lifts combined-tile survival from 0.53 to 0.98 at Earth and 0.80 to 0.99 at the Moon. In 3D RFT, soil training helps on Earth sand, on tiles and for rough-trained policies also on flat sand. On the stiffer lunar soil it helps only flat-trained Earth policies at Earth and changes the survival of Moon-trained policies by at most a few hundredths. In the sampled rollouts of the held-out soil models, Moon-trained policies keep most of their rigid-ground progress on lunar regolith at the low G1 foot pressure, with per-seed progress ratios of 0.84 to 1.39 apart from one seed with a short rigid reference. A gravity-randomized policy trained on rough 3D RFT terrain has a seed-mean survival of at least 0.84 at Earth and 0.96 at the Moon on every key test cell up to 20 degrees. Lunar results are simulation predictions conditional on the contact model and soil stiffness.

摘要（中文）：月球同时改变重力、地形和土壤。关于习得运动的研究，已在刚性地面上的低重力条件和地球重力下的颗粒地形中开展过，但尚未涉及同时在两种条件下的人形机器人、通用控制器迁移，或月球适应的地球成本。在仿真的Unitree G1平台上，我们使用同一套训练方案训练了12个策略，变化因素包括重力、地形几何形状和地面接触模型（刚性地面或三维阻力理论，3D RFT），并包含从地球到月球的微调以及重力随机化。我们在两种重力条件下的刚性地面和3D RFT环境中测试这些策略，并在其训练重力下对三种留出土壤模型进行测试。我们还仅在刚性地面上、两种重力条件下测试了冻结的SONIC——一个已发布的通用人形控制器。重力迁移具有不对称性。地球训练的策略在月球平坦刚性地面上的存活率保持在0.64至0.75之间，而月球训练及微调后的策略在地球上无法站立，SONIC在月球上的存活率最高仅为0.10。粗糙地形训练将组合瓦片地形的存活率在地球上从0.53提升至0.98，在月球上从0.80提升至0.99。在3D RFT环境中，土壤训练有助于地球沙地，对瓦片地形以及粗糙训练策略在平坦沙地也有帮助。在更硬的月球土壤上，它仅对地球平坦地形训练策略在地球上有帮助，而对月球训练策略的存活率影响至多只有几个百分点。在采样的留出土壤模型滚动测试中，月球训练策略在低G1足压下于月球风化层上保留了其在刚性地面上的大部分进展，各种子进展比率为0.84至1.39，只有一个种子因刚性参考较短而例外。一个在粗糙3D RFT地形上训练的重力随机化策略，在每一个关键测试单元（最高20度）上，地球种子平均存活率至少为0.84，月球上至少为0.96。月球结果是依赖于接触模型和土壤刚度的仿真预测。

Authors: Guillem Casadesus Vila, Sri Aditya Deevi, Grace X. Gao

Test-Time Motion Steering for Perceptive Humanoid Fall Recovery HumanoidEmbodied

humanoid fall recovery visual diffusion planner motion intent test-time steering recovery vocabulary

简要说明：RISE通过学习恢复词汇表并使用视觉扩散规划器根据任务成本预测运动意图，实现了在测试时引导人形机器人跌倒恢复，并在仿真和Unitree G1上进行了验证。

TLDR: RISE enables test-time steering of humanoid fall recovery by learning a recovery vocabulary and using a visual diffusion planner to predict motion intents guided by task costs, demonstrated in simulation and on a Unitree G1.

Abstract: Humanoid fall recovery requires selecting a motion that suits both the surrounding scene and the task. The same fallen pose can admit several ways to stand, with different routes, support transitions, and final headings. Yet reliable recovery alone does not provide control over which of these alternatives the robot executes. Steering this choice requires anticipating the physical consequences of a requested movement. We present RISE, an approach to perceptive humanoid recovery that lets task objectives steer how the robot returns to standing at inference time. It builds on two insights: diverse recoveries can be composed from shared movements, and anticipating how these movements unfold allows recovery to be steered toward a task objective. We learn a recovery vocabulary that connects intended movements to motor actions through sensory feedback. A visual diffusion planner learns from executions of this vocabulary to predict motion intent as future body states. Task costs guide this prediction toward a desired heading, rise speed, or path. The planner then generates motion latents conditioned on the steered intent, allowing the requested movement to shape its execution. Simulation experiments demonstrate diverse recoveries, terrain adaptation, and test-time steering without retraining, complemented by real-world demonstrations on a Unitree G1. Project page: https://osheraz.github.io/RISE/

摘要（中文）：类人机器人跌倒恢复需要在选择动作时同时兼顾周围场景与任务需求。相同的跌倒姿态可能存在多种起立方式，其路径、支撑转换及最终朝向各不相同。然而，仅实现可靠的恢复并不足以控制机器人执行其中哪一种方案。引导这一选择需要对所请求动作的物理后果进行预测。我们提出RISE方法，一种感知型类人机器人恢复方法，使任务目标能够在推理时引导机器人如何返回站立状态。该方法基于两个关键洞见：多样的恢复动作可由共享运动组合而成，且预测这些运动的展开方式可使恢复过程朝任务目标方向引导。我们学习了一个恢复动作词汇表，通过感觉反馈将意图运动与电机动作相连接。一个视觉扩散规划器通过学习该词汇表的执行记录，将运动意图预测为未来的身体状态。任务成本引导该预测朝向期望的朝向、起身速度或路径。随后，规划器在引导意图的条件下生成运动潜变量，使得所请求的动作能够塑造其执行过程。仿真实验展示了多样化的恢复动作、地形适应能力以及无需重新训练即可在测试时进行引导的特性，并在Unitree G1机器人上完成了真实世界演示验证。项目主页：https://osheraz.github.io/RISE/

Authors: Osher Azulay, Cheng-Lin Hsieh, Stella X. Yu

DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations Manipulation

bimanual tracking control human demonstrations proximal policy optimization behavioral cloning object-centered reward

简要说明：DONIC 提出了首个跨异构人类演示和操作类别的通用双手灵巧跟踪策略，通过结合 PPO 与行为克隆的反馈循环、以物体为中心的每手奖励和剪辑中心优势，在未见和未见物体上取得了最先进的成功率。

TLDR: DONIC introduces the first generalist bimanual dexterous tracking policy trained across heterogeneous human demonstrations and operation categories, using a feedback loop with PPO and behavioral cloning, object-centered per-hand rewards, and clip-centered advantages to achieve state-of-the-art success on unseen and held-out objects.

Abstract: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed. The scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data and the increased complexity of coordinating contacts make developing a generalist bimanual tracker particularly challenging. Therefore, we present 1) DONIC, the first generalist bimanual tracker jointly trained across operation categories and human-motion sources, together with 2) BiHOI, a multi-view dataset of 1,575 sequences spanning 229 objects and emphasizing sustained bimanual interaction, where reconstructed interactions are retargeted into robot references. DONIC combines proximal policy optimization with behavioral cloning in a feedback loop that recycles verified successful executions into training demonstrations. An object-centered per-hand reward maintains object-motion feedback while supervising each hand according to its reference contact role. Clip-Centered Advantages remove reference-dependent advantage offsets while preserving within-trajectory differences. Together, these designs enable one single policy to learn coordinated manipulation across heterogeneous references. Without finetuning, a single checkpoint achieves 86.79% success on unseen trajectories of training objects and 57.32% on held-out objects, surpassing the state-of-the-art bimanual tracking baselines by 77.36 and 45.73 percentage points.

摘要（中文）：尽管近期在灵巧参考跟踪方面取得了进展，现有模型主要聚焦于单手持物操作及有限范围的交互，未能涵盖现实生活中常见的双手灵巧行为。接触丰富的双手操作数据稀缺以及协调接触的复杂性增加，使得开发通用双手跟踪器尤为挑战。为此，我们提出：1) DONIC——首个跨操作类别和人体运动源联合训练的通用双手跟踪器，以及2) BiHOI——一个包含1575个序列、涵盖229个物体并强调持续双手交互的多视角数据集，其中重建的交互被重定向为机器人参考动作。DONIC将近端策略优化与行为克隆相结合，在反馈循环中将验证成功的执行重新循环为训练示范。以物体为中心的逐手奖励在根据参考接触角色监督每只手的同时，维持物体运动反馈。片段中心优势去除参考依赖的优势偏移，同时保留轨迹内差异。这些设计共同使单一策略能够跨异构参考学习协调操作。无需微调，单个检查点在训练物体的未见轨迹上达到86.79%的成功率，在保留物体上达到57.32%，分别超越最先进的双手跟踪基线77.36和45.73个百分点。

Authors: Mingze Sun, Ziang Cao, Yuan Fei, Qiankuan Tao, Zihan Wang, Tianqi Liu, Junhao Chen, Haiwen Diao, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Ziwei Liu

HuMiT: Low-Latency Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation via Compact Reference Tracking HumanoidEmbodied

whole-body teleoperation tracking policy low-latency humanoid robot sparse keypoints

简要说明：HuMiT提出了一种低延迟的全身人形远程操作系统，通过只使用紧凑参考目标（根部高度、根部速度和四个稀疏关键点的SE(3)姿态）的统一跟踪策略，实现了约20ms的通信到推理延迟，并在Unitree G1人形机器人上验证了接球等反应性任务。

TLDR: HuMiT presents a low-latency whole-body humanoid teleoperation system using a unified tracking policy with compact reference targets (root height, root velocity, and SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints), achieving ~20ms communication-to-inference latency and validated on a Unitree G1 humanoid for reactive tasks like catching a tossed ball.

Abstract: Real-time whole-body humanoid teleoperation remains challenging due to the computational latency introduced by optimization-based retargeting pipelines and future-frame conditioning. Existing motion tracking policies typically require dense reference targets including full joint positions, body-part transformations, and even future frames, which tightly couples the controller to expensive upstream modules. In this work, we present HuMiT, a whole-body teleoperation system built on a unified tracking policy that requires only a compact reference target, consisting of root height, root velocity, and the SE(3) poses of four sparse keypoints at the current frame, yet achieves competitive tracking fidelity compared to methods relying on more diverse reference states including complete joint positions, dense body-part transformations, and even future frames. Experiments show that our policy achieves a communication-to-inference latency of $\sim$20 ms measured between headset streaming and policy output and a video-based optical flow latency of 65 ms (median) across different motion types. We validate the system on a Unitree G1 humanoid, showcasing split-second reactive responses such as catching a tossed ball, as well as coordinated loco-manipulation capabilities. Project page: https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/.

摘要（中文）：实时全身人形遥操作仍面临挑战，主要源于基于优化的重定向流程及未来帧条件引入的计算延迟。现有运动跟踪策略通常需要稠密参考目标，包括完整关节位置、身体部位变换乃至未来帧，这使得控制器与昂贵的上游模块紧密耦合。在本工作中，我们提出HuMiT——一种基于统一跟踪策略的全身遥操作系统，该系统仅需一个紧凑参考目标，包含当前帧的根部高度、根部速度以及四个稀疏关键点的SE(3)位姿，却能达到与依赖更丰富参考状态（如完整关节位置、稠密身体部位变换乃至未来帧）的方法相媲美的跟踪保真度。实验表明，我们的策略在头戴设备流传输与策略输出之间实现了约20 ms的通信至推理延迟，并在不同类型动作下实现了65 ms（中位数）的基于视频的光流延迟。我们在Unitree G1人形机器人上验证了该系统，展示了诸如接住抛掷球等瞬间反应能力，以及协调的移动操作能力。项目页面：https://xiaohu-art.github.io/Track/。

Authors: Liu Cao, Botian Xu, Ruoqu Chen, Jiajun Liu, Mingzhi Pei, Zihao Wang, Zhongyu Li, Mengdi Xu

OMAR: Open-World Multi-Attribute Reasoning for Scene-Conditioned Shelf Organization Manipulation

open-world reasoning 3D scene graph vision-language model shelf organization object placement

简要说明：本文提出了一种开放世界多属性推理流水线，利用视觉语言模型和LLM推断潜在货架组织，并通过分割和多视图关联的3D场景图，实现新物体的合理放置。

TLDR: This paper presents an open-world multi-attribute reasoning pipeline that uses vision-language models and LLMs to infer latent shelf organization and place novel objects coherently in 3D scenes, grounded through segmentation and multi-view association.

Abstract: With the advent of foundation models, robots are increasingly capable of understanding and executing explicitly specified human tasks. Extending these capabilities to open-ended tasks, however, requires robots to infer appropriate actions from the observed scene. Household organization exemplifies this challenge, as robots must often act without detailed instructions, predefined object vocabularies, or known object-receptacle associations. While robots may follow instructions or learn organization preferences from demonstrations, inferring the latent organization of an occasionally changing scene and placing a novel object consistently with it remains challenging. We propose an open-world multi-attribute reasoning pipeline that grounds unknown objects across views and constructs an instance-level 3D scene graph for placement reasoning. First, a vision-language model proposes labels together with attributes such as content and packaging type, which are grounded through segmentation, depth, and multi-view association. Then, an LLM reasons over this representation to infer the latent shelf organization and rank scene-consistent object placements without explicitly user-provided preferences. The resulting placement rankings guide subsequent geometric and kinematic feasibility checks for execution. Our experimental evaluation shows that our approach leads to improved instance mapping and placement coherence over single-view language-grounding and geometry-only baselines, enabling autonomous placement of previously unseen objects without predefined object-receptacle mappings or class-specific retraining.

摘要（中文）：随着基础模型的出现，机器人日益能够理解和执行明确指定的人类任务。然而，将这些能力扩展到开放式任务，要求机器人能够从观察到的场景中推断出适当的行动。家居整理正是这一挑战的典型体现，因为机器人往往需要在没有详细指令、预定义物体词汇表或已知物体-容器关联的情况下采取行动。尽管机器人可以遵循指令或通过示范学习整理偏好，但对于一个偶尔发生变化的场景，推断其潜在整理规则并将新物体与之保持一致地放置，仍然是一项难题。我们提出了一种开放世界的多属性推理流水线，该流水线能够在不同视角下对未知物体进行 grounding，并构建实例级三维场景图以支持放置推理。首先，视觉-语言模型提出标签及内容物、包装类型等属性，并通过分割、深度信息和多视角关联进行 grounding。随后，大语言模型基于该表示进行推理，以推断潜在的货架整理规则，并在无需用户显式提供偏好的情况下，对场景一致的物体放置方案进行排序。所得到的放置排序进一步指导后续的几何与运动学可行性检查，以支持实际执行。我们的实验评估表明，相较于基于单视角语言 grounding 和仅依赖几何信息的基线方法，我们的方法在实例映射和放置一致性方面均有提升，能够在无需预定义物体-容器映射或针对特定类别重新训练的情况下，实现未知物体的自主放置。

Authors: Benedikt Kreis, Rohit Menon, Benno Wingender, Muhammad Ehsan Ullah, Nils Dengler, Maren Bennewitz

Post-hoc Epistemic Uncertainty for Vision-Language-Action Policies VLA

epistemic uncertainty VLA policies kernel variance heads Gaussian process LIBERO

简要说明：本文提出一种后验核方差头，从单一VLA策略的嵌入中估计认知不确定性，避免昂贵的集成，并在LIBERO-10上使用SmolVLA展示了在主动学习和监督参考等任务上与集成方法相当的性能。

TLDR: This paper proposes post-hoc kernel-variance heads to estimate epistemic uncertainty for VLA policies from a single policy's embeddings, avoiding expensive ensembles, and demonstrates competitive performance on LIBERO-10 with SmolVLA for tasks like active learning and supervision referral.

Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies need to recognize gaps in their training knowledge to request useful demonstrations or assistance in new situations, especially when failures are costly. Disagreement within an ensemble of independently trained policies can guide these decisions, but requires training and running multiple policies. We propose post-hoc kernel-variance heads that estimate epistemic uncertainty from the embeddings of a single policy. Each head computes the conditional variance of a Gaussian process conditioned on embeddings from the training demonstrations. Fitting requires no regression targets or gradient updates and leaves the policy unchanged. In experiments with SmolVLA on LIBERO-10, the kernel variance heads perform competitively with two-policy ensemble scores in task-level correlation with task success, in demonstration acquisition during active learning, and in referral to a stronger supervisor policy as a proxy for human assistance. For SmolVLA, the head on the vision-language backbone reduces uncertainty-scoring time by up to approximately a factor of 50 compared with ensemble scores, while also substantially reducing setup costs. We also show that the established evaluation protocol on LIBERO-10 primarily rewards recognition of coverage differences between tasks, while execution variability weakens assessment of within-task rankings. Thus, controlled perturbations provide a complementary evaluation: modality-specific heads identify unfamiliar camera, instruction, or state inputs, while fused heads can detect unfamiliar combinations of individually familiar inputs. With a supervisor proxy trained on the evaluated perturbation families, the decoder head improves within-task referral over ensemble disagreement. These findings show that useful uncertainty estimates for adaptive robot learning can be obtained from a single policy.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略需要识别其训练知识中的空白，以便在新情境中请求有用的演示或协助，尤其是在失败代价高昂的情况下。独立训练的策略集成之间的分歧可以指导这些决策，但需要训练和运行多个策略。我们提出了事后核方差头（post-hoc kernel-variance heads），通过单一策略的嵌入估计认知不确定性。每个头计算以训练演示嵌入为条件的高斯过程的条件方差。拟合过程无需回归目标或梯度更新，且不改变策略本身。在使用SmolVLA进行的LIBERO-10实验中，核方差头在任务级相关性与任务成功率、主动学习中的演示获取，以及作为人类协助代理的更强监督策略推荐方面，与双策略集成得分表现相当。对于SmolVLA，基于视觉-语言骨干网络的头将不确定性评分时间相比集成得分缩短了最多约50倍，同时大幅降低了设置成本。我们还表明，LIBERO-10上已有的评估协议主要奖励对任务间覆盖差异的识别，而执行变异性削弱了对任务内排序的评估。因此，受控扰动提供了一种补充性评估方式：模态特定头能够识别不熟悉的相机、指令或状态输入，而融合头能够检测单独熟悉输入的不熟悉组合。通过在评估的扰动族上训练监督代理，解码器头在任务内推荐方面优于集成分歧。这些发现表明，用于自适应机器人学习的有用的不确定性估计可以从单一策略中获得。

Authors: Johannes Keller, Albrecht M. Bloße, Adrian Lindenmeyer, Thomas Neumuth, Daniel Schneider

Reconstruction-Augmented Visuomotor Pre-Training of 3D-Grounded Bimanual Dexterity from RGB-Only Human Videos Manipulation

reconstruction-augmented pre-training 3D-grounded bimanual dexterity RGB-only human videos visuomotor pre-training scene geometry prediction

简要说明：SpatialDex通过从仅RGB人类视频中重建场景几何并将其作为策略输入和预测目标，学习3D基础的双臂灵巧操作，在模拟和真实世界任务上超越现有方法。

TLDR: SpatialDex learns 3D-grounded bimanual dexterity from RGB-only human videos by reconstructing scene geometry and using it as both policy input and prediction target, improving simulated and real-world dexterous manipulation over state-of-the-art.

Abstract: We present SpatialDex, a framework that learns 3D-grounded bimanual dexterity from RGB-only human videos through reconstruction-augmented visuomotor pre-training. The central idea is to learn human behavior together with its spatial context. From each video, we reconstruct the scene geometry and estimate the hand motion, align them at a shared video-level scale using the hand-size prior of 3D hand estimates. We retain the reconstructed geometry as both a policy input and a prediction target. The policy grounds the token grid of a pre-trained vision-language model in this geometry through gated residual fusion, is trained to predict future scene geometry alongside wrist and finger actions, and generates finger motion conditioned on the predicted trajectories of both wrists. Pre-trained on 1M human-video clips and fine-tuned with a small number of robot demonstrations, SpatialDex outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by 16.5 points on nine simulated dexterous tasks across two embodiments and by 38.3 points on six real-world bimanual dexterous tasks. Under a matched comparison, pre-training with reconstructed geometry improves success by 14.2 points over pre-training on hand motion alone.

摘要（中文）：我们提出了SpatialDex，一个通过重建增强的视觉运动预训练，从仅含RGB的人类视频中学习三维接地双手灵巧性的框架。其核心理念在于结合空间背景学习人类行为。针对每个视频，我们重建场景几何并估计手部运动，利用三维手部估计中的手部尺寸先验，在共享的视频级尺度上进行对齐。我们将重建的几何信息既作为策略输入，也作为预测目标。该策略通过门控残差融合将预训练视觉语言模型的令牌网格锚定在此几何信息上，训练目标是预测未来的场景几何以及手腕和手指的动作，并根据预测的双腕轨迹生成手指运动。在100万个人类视频片段上预训练，并通过少量机器人演示进行微调后，SpatialDex在两个仿真灵巧任务套装共九项任务上，相较于最先进方法平均提升了16.5个百分点；在六项真实世界双手灵巧任务中，则提升了38.3个百分点。在匹配对照实验中，相较于仅对手部动作进行预训练的方式，利用重建几何进行预训练可将成功率提升14.2个百分点。

Authors: Xingyi He, Zhiwen Qiu, Adhitya Polavaram, Yunhao Cao, Cory Fan, Julius Samwer, Saleh Kalantari, Kuan Fang

CausGround: Causal Interaction Grounding for Adaptive Embodied Planning Manipulation

causal interaction grounding embodied planning action preconditions and effects MLLM planning robot manipulation

简要说明：CausGround 是一种非参数化的因果交互接地框架，将交互经验提炼为以动作为中心的因果知识，通过将任务相关的因果依赖应用于当前观察，实现自适应的具身规划。它在模拟基准和真实机器人操作中提高了高层规划和交互推理能力，且无需参数更新。

TLDR: CausGround is a non-parametric causal interaction grounding framework that distills interaction experience into action-centered causal knowledge, enabling adaptive embodied planning by grounding task-relevant causal dependencies in current observations. It improves high-level planning and interaction reasoning on simulated benchmarks and real-world robot manipulation without parameter updates.

Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show promising reasoning capabilities, but reliable physical interaction requires planning that accounts for when actions are executable and how they change the world. These preconditions and effects are environment-dependent and often not captured by MLLMs, making adaptation challenging. Yet existing approaches either require costly environment-specific training or rely on unstructured interaction experience that is difficult to reuse. Therefore, we introduce CausGround, a non-parametric causal interaction grounding framework that distills interaction experience into reusable action-centered causal knowledge. CausGround identifies action preconditions and effects and organizes them in a factorized world-state representation capturing object attributes and inter-object relations. At planning time, task-relevant causal dependencies are grounded in current observations to support backward reasoning over preconditions and forward reasoning over effects for action selection and multi-step planning. We evaluate CausGround on simulated high-level planning, interaction reasoning, and real-world robot manipulation. On adapted VirtualHome and RoboCasa benchmarks, CausGround improves vision-based high-level planning across MLLM backbones, increasing average task success from 24.9% to 53.3% on VirtualHome and closed-loop planning success from 43.0% to 57.0% on RoboCasa. On SWITCH, average interaction reasoning accuracy increases from 25.8% to 31.9%, indicating improved action selection, recovery, and verification. Moreover, real-world experiments show that CausGround reasons backward from MLLM-interpreted goals to derive executable high-level action sequences for sequential manipulation. These results demonstrate that reusable action preconditions and effects support long-horizon embodied planning across diverse environments without parameter updates.

摘要（中文）：多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）展现出令人瞩目的推理能力，但可靠的身体交互需要规划，这种规划需考虑动作何时可执行以及动作如何改变世界。这些前提条件和效果依赖于环境，往往无法被多模态大语言模型所捕获，这使得适应性调整颇具挑战。然而，现有方法要么需要代价高昂的特定环境训练，要么依赖于难以复用的非结构化交互经验。为此，我们提出了CausGround，一种非参数化因果交互基础框架，将交互经验提炼为可复用的以动作为中心的因果知识。CausGround识别动作前提条件和效果，并将其组织在分解的世界状态表示中，以捕获对象属性和对象间关系。在规划阶段，与任务相关的因果依赖关系被锚定在当前观测中，以支持对前提条件的反向推理和对效果的正向推理，从而实现动作选择和多步规划。我们在模拟高层规划、交互推理和真实机器人操作上评估了CausGround。在适配的VirtualHome和RoboCasa基准测试中，CausGround提升了基于视觉的高层规划在不同多模态大语言模型骨干上的表现，将VirtualHome上的平均任务成功率从24.9%提高到53.3%，将RoboCasa上的闭环规划成功率从43.0%提高到57.0%。在SWITCH上，平均交互推理准确率从25.8%提高到31.9%，表明动作选择、恢复和验证能力得到增强。此外，真实世界实验表明，CausGround能够从多模态大语言模型解释的目标出发进行反向推理，从而为顺序操作推导出可执行的高层动作序列。这些结果表明，可复用的动作前提条件和效果能够在无需参数更新的情况下，支持跨多种环境的长时间跨度具身规划。

Authors: Yijun Shen, Diqi He, Jinbang Guo, Wanyue Zhang, Jiaming Mi, Huan Yang, Zhongyuan Wang, Zhiwei Yu, Kai Zhang

Watch Your Step: Anticipated Perception for Humanoid Locomotion Locomotion

foothold prediction elevation map sampling perceptive locomotion humanoid robot zero-shot transfer

简要说明：本文提出一种轻量级足部着地点预测模型，仅围绕预测的未来足部位置采样地形高程图，使感知运动策略训练更快、泛化更强，并零样本迁移到真实Unitree G1人形机器人。

TLDR: This paper introduces a lightweight foothold prediction model that samples terrain elevation maps only around predicted future footholds, enabling perceptive locomotion policies to train faster and generalize better, with zero-shot transfer to a real Unitree G1 humanoid.

Abstract: Perceptive locomotion policies typically observe a dense robot-centric elevation map, although only the terrain beneath and around the next footsteps informs the control decision. Learned encoders compress the whole visual input, leaving the policy to work out which inputs matter while learning the baseline locomotion task. Learning both at once slows training and, without computationally expensive attention mechanisms, makes generalization to new terrain harder. We instead remove redundant inputs from the elevation map before the policy sees it. A lightweight foothold prediction model (FPM) predicts future footholds from proprioception and the velocity command alone, and we sample the elevation map only in small patches around these predicted footholds. We train the prediction model alongside the locomotion policy, periodically retraining it on new policy rollouts as the robot's gait matures. This allows the perception to anticipate where the policy will step, while the policy learns to leverage terrain information around those steps. With the proposed lightweight preprocessing, the policy reaches a given terrain difficulty in roughly a third of the training iterations required with the complete map. It outperforms policies that observe the complete map where footholds are sparse, including in narrow walled corridors, and on unseen terrain, and it matches an attention-based encoder trained at several times the cost. The policy transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid traversing various obstacles, stairs, gaps, and step-downs beyond the training distribution in both indoor and outdoor environments.

摘要（中文）：感知型运动策略通常观察密集的以机器人为中心的高程图，尽管实际上只有下一个落脚点下方及其周围的地形才影响控制决策。学习型编码器压缩整个视觉输入，让策略在学习基线运动任务的同时自行判断哪些输入是重要的。同时学习这两项任务会拖慢训练速度，并且在缺乏计算开销较高的注意力机制的情况下，会使策略更难泛化到新地形。我们转而在地形图输入到策略之前就去除冗余信息。一个轻量级的落脚点预测模型（FPM）仅利用本体感觉和速度指令来预测未来落脚点，而我们仅在这些预测落脚点周围的小块区域中对高程图进行采样。我们让预测模型与运动策略联合训练，并随着机器人步态逐渐成熟，周期性地在新策略的轨迹数据上对其重新训练。这使得感知模块能够预判策略将要在哪里落脚，同时策略也学会利用这些落脚点周围的地形信息。通过所提出的轻量级预处理，策略在达到给定的地形难度时，所需的训练迭代次数约为使用完整地图时的三分之一。在落脚点稀疏的场景中（包括狭窄的围墙走廊）以及未见过的地形上，该策略均优于观察完整地图的策略，并且与一个训练成本高数倍的基于注意力的编码器表现相当。该策略可零样本迁移到宇树G1人形机器人上，使其在室内和室外环境中穿越超出训练分布的各种障碍物、楼梯、缝隙和台阶下坡。

Authors: Matthias Heyrman, Chenhao Li, Ioannis Dadiotis, Marco Hutter

From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation VLA

VLA models self-evolving history-dependent manipulation harness hierarchical architecture

简要说明：本文提出SERA，一种自进化框架，通过可更新的任务上下文和规划增强固定的VLA执行器，在RoboMME基准上提升了历史依赖操作任务的性能。

TLDR: This paper proposes SERA, a self-evolving harness that augments a fixed VLA executor with updatable task context and planning, improving history-dependent manipulation performance on the RoboMME benchmark.

Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation. However, long-horizon tasks can involve non-Markovian dependencies: successful decisions may require retaining task progress and past interaction outcomes, while partial observability and execution errors compound over time. Existing work has begun to address these challenges by augmenting foundation-model policies with memory and by introducing hierarchical architectures that separate high-level planning from low-level execution. We organize the high-level VLM as a robotic agent through an editable harness to maintain task context and improve planning through execution experience. We instantiate this approach as SERA (Self-Evolving Robotic Agent), with a fixed VLA executor providing low-level control. The harness maintains and updates task context using observations and execution feedback to guide subsequent planning. Self-evolution uses environment rollouts to propose and evaluate harness revisions, with the selected configuration fixed before held-out testing. On RoboMME, SERA achieves 51.38% overall success with autonomous selection, compared with 44.38% without self-evolution. Our exploration suggests that agentic planning is a promising direction for history-dependent robotic manipulation.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型通过统一视觉理解、语言条件与动作生成，在具身操作任务中展现出强劲性能。然而，长时程任务可能涉及非马尔可夫依赖：成功决策往往需要保留任务进度及过往交互结果，同时部分可观测性与执行误差会随时间累积。现有工作已开始通过为基础模型策略增设记忆机制，以及引入将高层规划与低层执行分离的层级架构来应对上述挑战。我们通过一个可编辑的调控框架（harness）将高层视觉语言模型组织为机器人智能体，以维持任务上下文，并通过执行经验改进规划。我们将该方法实例化为SERA（自进化机器人智能体，Self-Evolving Robotic Agent），由固定的VLA执行器提供低层控制。调控框架利用观测与执行反馈来维护和更新任务上下文，以指导后续规划。自进化机制通过环境回滚提出并评估调控框架的修订方案，选定的配置在保留测试前固定。在RoboMME基准上，SERA在自主选择配置下实现了51.38%的总体成功率，而未采用自进化时仅为44.38%。我们的探索表明，智能体式规划是面向历史依赖型机器人操作的一个有前景的方向。

Authors: Tingwen Du, Haoyu Guo, Hanxue Zhang, Xuanxu Wang, Junting Dong, Chao Gao, Mingfei Han, Tao Lu, Mulin Yu, Chunhua Shen, Xiaojun Chang, Zhihui Li

Distance Field Driven Reinforcement Learning for Reactive and Robust Collision Avoidance Manipulation

Reinforcement Learning Euclidean Distance Field Collision Avoidance Sim-to-Real Transfer Manipulator

简要说明：本文提出了一种将欧氏距离场直接集成到观测空间中的强化学习框架，用于7自由度机械臂，实现了零样本仿真到实物的迁移，并能稳健地避开静态和动态障碍物。

TLDR: This paper presents an RL framework that integrates Euclidean Distance Fields into the observation space for a 7-DoF manipulator, achieving zero-shot sim-to-real transfer and robust collision avoidance against static and dynamic obstacles.

Abstract: Robust and reactive collision avoidance remains a central challenge for deploying Reinforcement Learning (RL) policies on real robotic manipulators, particularly when transferring behaviours learned in simulation to the physical world. This paper presents an RL framework that integrates the Euclidean Distance Field (EDF) directly into the observation space, providing the agent with continuous geometric cues that support stable and responsive avoidance behaviours. By leveraging the rich spatial information encoded in the EDF, the method enables a streamlined reward formulation that achieves effective obstacle avoidance both with and without Artificial Potential Field guidance. The proposed approach is validated on a 7-DoF redundant manipulator, demonstrating zero-shot transfer from simulation to real hardware. Despite being trained exclusively with randomised static objects, the deployed policy generalizes to previously unseen real environments and exhibits robust online avoidance of dynamic obstacles. These results highlight the potential of EDF-based representations to mitigate the sim-to-real gap and support reliable and real-time collision-aware behaviour in complex and changing environments.

摘要（中文）：摘要：鲁棒且反应式的碰撞避免仍是将强化学习（RL）策略部署到真实机器人操作臂上的核心挑战，尤其是在将仿真中学习到的行为迁移至物理世界时。本文提出了一种强化学习框架，将欧氏距离场（EDF）直接融入观测空间，为智能体提供连续的几何线索，以支持稳定且灵敏的避障行为。通过利用EDF中蕴含的丰富空间信息，该方法实现了简化的奖励设计，并可在有无人工势场引导的情况下均能有效完成避障任务。所提方法在七自由度冗余机械臂上进行了验证，展示了从仿真到真实硬件的零样本迁移能力。尽管仅在随机静态物体上训练，部署后的策略仍能泛化至未见过的真实环境，并对动态障碍物表现出鲁棒的在线避障能力。这些结果凸显了基于EDF的表示在缩小仿真与真实差距、以及在复杂动态环境中支持可靠且实时的碰撞感知行为方面的潜力。

Authors: Taiga Ikeshima, Sheila Sutjipto, Lan Wu, Francisco J. Naranjo-Campos, Taiki Ishigaki, Taisuke Kobayashi, Teresa A. Vidal-Calleja, Eiichi Yoshida

A2I-Calib++: A Kinematics-Driven Anti-noise Active Calibration Framework for Whole-Body Multi-IMU Systems on Legged Robots Locomotion

multi-IMU calibration legged robot active calibration kinematics-driven anti-noise

简要说明：本文提出了一种运动学驱动的主动标定框架，用于四足机器人多IMU系统的标定，通过轨迹优化、对抗运动先验和接触约束虚拟IMU解决激励不足和噪声问题，提升标定精度和里程计性能。

TLDR: This paper presents a kinematics-driven active calibration framework for multi-IMU systems on legged robots, addressing excitation and noise challenges through trajectory optimization, adversarial motion priors, and contact-constrained virtual IMUs to improve calibration accuracy and odometry.

Abstract: Recently, multi-node inertial measurement unit (multi-IMU) systems have shown promise for robust odometry in legged robots. Multi-IMU fusion can improve legged robot odometry but requires accurate spatiotemporal calibration among the sensors. Existing multi-IMU calibration methods, designed for aerial or handheld platforms, face challenges on legged robots because routine locomotion may provide insufficient excitation, while foot slips, impacts, and vibrations introduce measurement disturbances. To address these challenges, we propose A2I-Calib++, a kinematics-driven anti-noise active calibration framework for body-mounted IMUs covered by the robot kinematic model. It estimates temporal offsets, extrinsic rotations and translations, and inertial biases through temporal correlation search followed by analytic spatial and bias estimation, without artificial calibration targets or complex parameter tuning for the target IMU. A2I-Calib++ comprises three core modules: 1) a Noise-Isotropy-Inspired Trajectory supported by a finite-horizon conditioning proposition that generates sufficient excitation to limit noise sensitivity; 2) a constraint-aware Adversarial Motion Priors controller that combines the anti-noise excitation with a rolling-contact reward for contact-aware execution; and 3) a contact-constrained virtual IMU that fuses pre-calibrated calf IMUs and joint kinematics under a rolling-contact model to construct the calibration reference. Furthermore, evaluations on both simulation and real-world quadruped platforms demonstrate notably reduced noise sensitivity and simulation calibration errors compared to conventional methods, together with repeatable real-world calibration and improved proprioceptive odometry accuracy for legged robots.

摘要（中文）：近期，多节点惯性测量单元（multi-IMU）系统在腿足机器人的鲁棒里程计方面展现出良好前景。多IMU融合能够提升腿足机器人的里程计性能，但需要传感器之间精确的时空标定。现有的多IMU标定方法主要针对空中或手持平台设计，在腿足机器人上应用面临挑战，因为常规运动可能激励不足，而足部打滑、冲击和振动会引入测量干扰。为应对这些挑战，我们提出A2I-Calib++，一种运动学驱动的抗噪声主动标定框架，适用于机器人运动学模型覆盖的机体安装IMU。该方法通过时间相关性搜索后进行解析空间与偏置估计，估计时间偏移、外参旋转和平移及惯性偏置，无需人工标定目标或对目标IMU进行复杂参数调节。A2I-Calib++包含三个核心模块：1）一种基于噪声各向同性启发的轨迹，辅以有限时域条件性命题，产生充分激励以限制噪声敏感性；2）一种约束感知的对抗性运动先验控制器，将抗噪声激励与滚动接触奖励相结合，实现接触感知执行；3）一种接触约束的虚拟IMU，在滚动接触模型下融合预先标定的小腿IMU和关节运动学，构建标定参考。此外，在仿真和实际四足平台上的评估表明，与传统方法相比，该方法显著降低了噪声敏感性和仿真标定误差，同时实现了可重复的实际标定结果，并提升了腿足机器人的本体感觉里程计精度。

Authors: Fangyu Jiang, Chaoran Xiong, Kehui Ma, Zhen Sun, Zeyu Zhang, Ling Pei

PRISM: Learning Realistic Depth via Physics-Grounded Noise Disentanglement with Semantic-Geometric Collaboration RLRobot

depth noise synthesis sim-to-real transfer physics-grounded noise disentanglement 3D visual foundation model robotic manipulation

简要说明：PRISM 提出一种物理驱动的深度噪声解耦框架，将真实深度传感器噪声分离为感知失效和测量误差，利用3D视觉基础模型先验与层级监督生成逼真噪声深度，将真实机器人操作成功率提升至92.1%。

TLDR: PRISM is a physics-grounded framework that disentangles real-world depth sensor noise into sensing invalidation and measurement inaccuracy, using 3D visual foundation model priors and hierarchical supervision to synthesize realistic noisy depth, improving sim-to-real robotic manipulation success to 92.1%.

Abstract: Real-world physical sensing exhibits complex, heterogeneous noise patterns that deviate significantly from idealized simulation, posing a fundamental bottleneck for sim-to-real transfer. Existing sensor modelings typically treat depth noise as a monolithic black-box process, overlooking the distinct physical mechanisms that govern different error modalities. In this work, we introduce a physics-grounded paradigm that disentangles monolithic noise into two complementary modalities: \textbf{sensing invalidation} and \textbf{measurement inaccuracy}, enabling a tailored treatment of noise sources based on their physical origins. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{PRISM}, a tripartite framework that distills 3D Visual Foundation Model features as rich spatial-semantic priors for physics-based reasoning. To address the inherent sparsity and class imbalance of invalidation regions, we develop Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision, integrating multi-scale positive-weighted objectives with a positive-preserving dynamic hard mining strategy to enforce precise artifact delineation. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves state-of-the-art fidelity in noisy depth synthesis. Furthermore, downstream robotic experiments show that PRISM facilitates a \textbf{92.1\%} average success rate in the real world, marking a significant improvement over monolithic baselines. Our project page is available at: \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\href{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}.}

摘要（中文）：真实世界的物理感知呈现出复杂且异构的噪声模式，与理想化仿真环境存在显著偏差，这构成了模拟到现实迁移的根本性瓶颈。现有传感器建模通常将深度噪声视为一个整体式黑盒过程，忽视了支配不同误差模态的独特物理机制。在本工作中，我们引入了一种基于物理学的范式，将整体式噪声解耦为两种互补模态：**感知失效**与**测量不精确**，从而能够根据噪声源的物理起源对其进行针对性处理。基于这一洞见，我们提出**PRISM**——一个三元框架，将三维视觉基础模型特征蒸馏为丰富的空间-语义先验，用于基于物理的推理。为解决失效区域固有的稀疏性与类别不平衡问题，我们开发了层次化正样本优先监督方法，将多尺度正样本加权目标与正样本保留动态难例挖掘策略相结合，以实现伪影的精确描绘。大量基准测试表明，PRISM在噪声深度合成中达到了最先进的保真度。此外，下游机器人实验显示，PRISM在真实世界中实现了**92.1%**的平均成功率，较整体式基线方法有显著提升。我们的项目页面可在以下网址访问：\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\href{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}。}

Authors: Xiujian Liang, Jiacheng Liu, Mingyang Sun, Qichen He, Anda Cheng, Cewu Lu, Jianhua Sun

Plan First, Act Later: Streaming Reasoning for Executable Memory in Robot Control VLA

hierarchical memory long-horizon manipulation vision-language-action subtask_list self-labeling

简要说明：PAL提出了一个分层记忆框架，通过高层VLM主动生成可执行的子任务列表，提升了长时程机器人操作的成功率。

TLDR: PAL introduces a hierarchical memory framework with a high-level VLM that proactively writes an executable subtask list for long-horizon robot manipulation, improving success rates on benchmarks and real-world tasks.

Abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires a robot to remember task-relevant information beyond its short observation window. Existing memory-augmented policies typically retrieve relevant information from history and reason over it at execution time, placing a heavy reasoning burden on the high-level model. To address this challenge, we propose PAL (\textbf{P}lan first, \textbf{A}ct \textbf{L}ater), a hierarchical memory framework for vision-language robot manipulation. It maintains a short-term visual buffer, a semantic-event memory, and an executable \texttt{subtask\_list}. A high-level vision-language model (VLM) converts streaming visual observations into the \texttt{subtask\_list}. At execution time, the VLM selects the currently relevant subtask from the \texttt{subtask\_list} and passes it to a low-level vision-language-action (VLA) policy. To teach the model what to write to memory and when to update it, we introduce a two-stage data generation procedure that first expands sparse update supervision and then uses self-labeling with task-grounded verification to generate training data that better match the state distribution encountered during execution. We evaluate our approach on memory-dependent benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks. On RoboMME, PAL achieves a \textbf{56.05\%} success rate, outperforming the strongest baseline, FrameSamp-Modul, at 44.51\%. In real-world experiments across four manipulation tasks, \pal{} reaches \textbf{60.83\%} overall success, surpassing MemER (45.00\%) and FrameSamp-Modul (28.33\%). These results show that proactively writing future-relevant subtasks into hierarchical memory improves long-horizon visual reasoning and robot control. Code and videos can be found on our website: https://qinghangliu.github.io/pal-webpage/

摘要（中文）：长期机器人操控要求机器人记住其短暂观察窗口之外的任务相关信息。现有的记忆增强策略通常在执行时从历史记录中检索相关信息并进行推理，这给高层模型带来了沉重的推理负担。为应对这一挑战，我们提出了PAL（**P**lan first, **A**ct **L**ater），一种面向视觉语言机器人操控的分层记忆框架。该框架维护一个短期视觉缓冲区、一个语义事件记忆以及一个可执行的\texttt{subtask\_list}。高层视觉语言模型（VLM）将流式视觉观察转换为\texttt{subtask\_list}。在执行时，VLM从\texttt{subtask\_list}中选择当前相关的子任务，并将其传递给低层视觉语言动作（VLA）策略。为了教会模型在何时写入何种记忆内容以及何时更新记忆，我们引入了一种两阶段数据生成流程：首先扩展稀疏的更新监督，然后使用基于任务验证的自标注方法生成更贴合执行时状态分布的训练数据。我们在依赖记忆的基准测试和真实世界操控任务上评估了我们的方法。在RoboMME上，PAL达到了\textbf{56.05\%}的成功率，超过了最强基线FrameSamp-Modul的44.51\%。在四项真实世界操控任务中，PAL取得了\textbf{60.83\%}的整体成功率，优于MemER（45.00\%）和FrameSamp-Modul（28.33\%）。这些结果表明，将未来相关的子任务主动写入分层记忆能够提升长期视觉推理和机器人控制性能。代码和视频可在我们的网站上获取：https://qinghangliu.github.io/pal-webpage/

Authors: Qinghang Liu, Conglin Wang, Zongsheng Li, Boyong He, Han Gao, Pengcheng Wang, Tao Sun, Lige Liu, Chang Liu

Relational Geometry Forcing for World Action Models WorldModel

World Action Models Relational Geometry Forcing 3D foundation model feature relation alignment robot manipulation

简要说明：本文提出关系几何强制（RGF），一种仅训练时的方法，通过对齐成对特征关系而非逐点特征，将冻结的3D基础模型的几何先验迁移到世界动作模型，从而提升操作性能且不增加推理模块。

TLDR: This paper proposes Relational Geometry Forcing (RGF), a training-only method that transfers geometric priors from a frozen 3D foundation model to World Action Models by aligning pairwise feature relations rather than pointwise features, improving manipulation performance without adding inference-time modules.

Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have shown strong potential for robot manipulation by jointly learning visual dynamics and executable actions. However, their video and action objectives do not explicitly constrain the 3D geometry that is crucial for precise manipulation. Recently, geometry-aware WAMs introduce depth or 4D prediction branches, whereas representation alignment methods supervise intermediate WAM features with pretrained 3D foundation models. Yet we find that such pointwise alignment benefits the video features but degrades action learning, since dense geometric feature targets overly restrict compact action features. To address this limitation, we propose Relational Geometry Forcing (RGF), which transfers geometric priors from a frozen 3D foundation model by aligning pairwise feature relations instead of pointwise features. Specifically, RGF applies three complementary relational objectives, where intra-frame and cross-view relations transfer scene geometry and multi-view correspondence to the video features, while action-temporal relations couple action dynamics to geometric scene evolution. Applied only during training, RGF requires no explicit geometry branch or extra inference module. Extensive experiments in simulation and the real world demonstrate the effectiveness of Relational Geometry Forcing, showing consistent gains across diverse manipulation scenarios and WAM paradigms.

摘要（中文）：世界动作模型（WAMs）通过联合学习视觉动态与可执行动作，在机器人操作中展现出强大潜力。然而，其视频与动作目标并未显式约束对于精确操作至关重要的三维几何结构。近期，几何感知的世界动作模型引入了深度或四维预测分支，而表示对齐方法则利用预训练的三维基础模型监督WAM中间特征。但我们发现，这种逐点对齐虽有益于视频特征，却反而损害了动作学习，因为密集的几何特征目标过度限制了紧凑的动作特征。为解决这一局限，我们提出了关系几何约束（RGF），通过对齐成对特征关系而非逐点特征，从冻结的三维基础模型中迁移几何先验。具体而言，RGF施加了三种互补的关系目标：帧内与跨视角关系将场景几何和多视角对应关系迁移至视频特征，而动作-时间关系则将动作动态与几何场景演化相耦合。RGF仅在训练期间使用，无需显式几何分支或额外推理模块。在仿真与真实世界中的大量实验验证了关系几何约束的有效性，显示出在多种操作场景和WAM范式下的一致性能提升。

Authors: Yuan Xu, Yixiang Chen, Qisen Ma, Jiabing Yang, Peiyan Li, Kai Wang, Jianhua Yang, Jianlou Si, Jun Huang, Jing Liu, Nianfeng Liu, Yan Huang, Liang Wang

Training in Deployment: Human-in-the-loop Online Post-Training for Robot Manipulation Manipulation

human-in-the-loop online post-training manipulation provenance-conditioned learning bimanual tasks

简要说明：TIDE提出了一种人在回路的在线后训练系统，用于机器人操作，通过基于数据来源条件的监督学习利用部署数据，避免使用学习的评论家或奖励模型，并在真实世界双臂任务中在一小时内提升任务完成率。

TLDR: TIDE presents a human-in-the-loop online post-training system for robot manipulation that uses provenance-conditioned supervised learning on deployment data, avoiding learned critics or reward models, and improves task completion in real-world bimanual tasks within under an hour per task.

Abstract: Large pretrained robot foundation models provide strong priors for manipulation, yet adapting them to target tasks with offline teleoperated demonstrations often fails to cover the contact-rich, recovery, and precision-critical states encountered during deployment. Existing methods mitigate this issue by augmenting offline demonstrations with human-in-the-loop data or online reinforcement learning. Despite this, offline post-training adapts slowly because it cannot immediately absorb deployment experience, while online RL typically relies on value functions or auxiliary actor-critic models, increasing both training complexity and instability. We present TIDE (Training In DEployment), a human-in-the-loop online post-training system. TIDE introduces a provenance-conditioned supervised learning framework that updates the policy online from human interventions and policy-generated rollouts collected during deployment, without a learned critic, reward model, or action scorer. Across four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, TIDE improves milestone-normalized task progress and binary full-task completion over the warm-start policy and matched additional offline demonstrations, and performs comparably to the fixed-policy collection baseline while making updated checkpoints available during deployment. Each task-specific online post-training session, from the start of deployment rollouts until the final checkpoint is available, completes in less than one hour while learning and checkpoint handling run asynchronously.

摘要（中文）：大型预训练机器人基础模型为操作任务提供了强大的先验知识，然而，将其适配到目标任务时，离线遥操作演示往往无法覆盖部署过程中遇到的接触密集、恢复及高精度关键状态。现有方法通过引入人在回路数据或在线强化学习来增强离线演示，从而缓解这一问题。尽管如此，离线后训练由于无法即时吸收部署经验而收敛缓慢，而在线强化学习通常依赖价值函数或辅助的演员-评论家模型，增加了训练复杂度与不稳定性。我们提出了TIDE（Training In DEployment，部署中训练），一种人在回路的在线后训练系统。TIDE引入了一种基于来源条件化的监督学习框架，直接从部署期间收集的人类干预及策略生成的轨迹中在线更新策略，无需学习批评者、奖励模型或动作评分器。在四个真实世界的双臂操作任务中，TIDE在里程碑归一化任务进展和二元全任务完成率上均优于热启动策略及匹配的额外离线演示，并且在部署过程中提供更新的检查点，同时与固定策略收集基线表现相当。从部署轨迹开始到最终检查点可用，每个任务特定的在线后训练会话在一小时内完成，且学习与检查点处理异步运行。

Authors: Chun Gu, Xiaofei Wei, Yiming Chen, Bozhou Zhang, Juntong Zhang, Xiatian Zhu, Li Zhang

DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation Manipulation

joint-embedding predictive architecture RGB-D perception depth-grounded state representation action-conditioned prediction robot manipulation

简要说明：DepState-JEPA 是一种双流 RGB-深度联合嵌入预测架构，通过度量 3D 接地和动作条件预测学习共享潜在状态，从而提升机器人操作的视觉预测和策略学习。

TLDR: DepState-JEPA is a dual-stream RGB-depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that learns a depth-grounded shared latent state for robot manipulation, improving visual forecasting and policy learning by integrating metric 3D grounding and action-conditioned prediction.

Abstract: Predictive representations for robot manipulation should connect scene geometry with the state changes induced by actions. Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes. Guided by this intuition, we introduce \textbf{DepState-JEPA}, a dual-stream RGB--Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, \textbf{DepState}. Built on V-JEPA~2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding. Ray-conditioned readouts predict local features without target depth; after an action-conditioned transition, the same decoders predict future RGB and depth features using the predicted state and fixed initial private features. Robot-state readouts provide recursive proprioceptive inputs; object-trajectory supervision and calibrated forward kinematics shape state learning through motion targets and joint--TCP consistency. Comparisons show stronger RGB-encoder transfer after RGB-D adaptation, feature completion, conditioned visual forecasting, and manipulation success. Within-model ablations identify contributions from depth content, metric coordinates, and future-state matching, with additional control gains from FK regularization.

摘要（中文）：预测性表征在机器人操作中应当将场景几何结构与动作引发的状态变化联系起来。我们的直觉是，理解一个动作将改变什么，始于理解事物在哪里：互补的RGB与深度观测共同锚定了一个统一的场景表征，从中可以推断这些变化。在这一直觉的引导下，我们提出了\textbf{DepState-JEPA}，一种双流RGB-深度联合嵌入预测架构，通过共享潜在状态\textbf{DepState}将空间理解与动作条件预测连接起来。该框架基于V-JEPA~2.1，将深度既作为互补的观测流，又用于将两种模态锚定在度量三维空间中，将共享信息聚合到DepState中，同时保留各模态私有的特征用于解码。射线条件化读取无需目标深度即可预测局部特征；在动作条件化转换之后，相同的解码器利用预测状态和固定的初始私有特征预测未来的RGB与深度特征。机器人状态读取提供递归的本体感觉输入；物体轨迹监督与标定正向运动学通过运动目标和关节-末端执行器一致性塑造状态学习。对比实验表明，在RGB-D适应、特征补全、条件化视觉预测和操作成功率方面，RGB编码器的迁移性能更强。模型内部的消融实验识别出深度内容、度量坐标和未来状态匹配的贡献，同时FK正则化带来了额外的控制增益。

Authors: Xiujian Liang, Liuyuan Na, Zehao Du, Jiacheng Xu, Weixi Song, Mingyang Sun, Xingjun Ma, Cewu Lu, Jianhua Sun

NavBind: Diagnosing Instruction-Action Binding at Route Forks in Navigation VLAs VLA

instruction-action binding navigation VLA route-fork contexts R2R-CE RxR-CE

简要说明：本文提出NavBind，一种用于导航VLA模型的诊断方法，通过在路径分岔情境中改变指令来评估动作分布是否随之变化，揭示成功指标并不保证模型真正遵循指令。

TLDR: This paper introduces NavBind, a diagnostic method for navigation VLA models that evaluates whether changing instructions alters action distributions in route-fork contexts, revealing that success metrics do not guarantee instruction following.

Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) navigation models translate visual observations and instructions into actions. Navigation success assesses whether an agent reaches the goal. However, reaching the goal successfully does not establish whether the model genuinely follows the instructions or relies on visual cues or navigation history. We introduce NavBind to diagnose instruction-action binding: whether changing the instruction influences the probabilistic distribution of the actions, with the navigation context fixed. We construct 3,252 route-fork contexts by recombining route-aligned instruction segments from R2R-CE and RxR-CE. Each context pairs full instructions that share the description of the route already traveled but specify different branches. Both are evaluated under the same agent state and navigation history. We compare generated local action sequences, the likelihoods of fixed reference action sequences under both instructions, and changes in visual attention and attribution. Across the evaluated models, higher reported navigation success does not imply that the model more faithfully follows the instructions.

摘要（中文）：视觉-语言-动作（VLA）导航模型将视觉观察与指令转化为行动。导航成功评估的是智能体是否到达目标。然而，成功到达目标并不能证明模型真正遵循了指令，还是依赖视觉线索或导航历史。我们引入NavBind来诊断指令-动作绑定关系：即，在导航上下文不变的情况下，更改指令是否会影响动作的概率分布。我们通过重组R2R-CE和RxR-CE中与路线对齐的指令片段，构建了3，252个路线分叉上下文。每个上下文将完整指令配对，这些指令共享已行驶路线的描述，但指定不同的分支。两者均在相同的智能体状态和导航历史下进行评估。我们比较了生成的局部动作序列、在两条指令下固定参考动作序列的似然性，以及视觉注意力和归因的变化。在所评估的模型中，较高的导航成功报告率并不意味模型更忠实地遵循指令。

Authors: Josh Qixuan Sun, Xiaoying Xing, Yurun Chen, Huaiyuan Weng, Wentao Zhu, Mark Crowley

SMR: Learning streaming motion retargeting for humanoids from human semantic HumanoidEmbodied

motion retargeting humanoid robots physics experts causal Transformer whole-body control

简要说明：本文提出了SMR，一种用于人形机器人的流式动作重定向方法，从语义条件物理专家中学习，将人体动作转换为机器人感知的任务空间目标，并训练因果Transformer生成下游全身控制的机器人运动参考。

TLDR: This paper presents SMR, a streaming neural motion retargeter for humanoid robots that learns from semantic-conditioned physics experts, converting human motion into robot-aware task-space targets and training a causal Transformer to generate robot motion references for downstream whole-body control.

Abstract: Retargeting human motion to humanoids requires preserving motion semantics while accounting for the robot's physical constraints. Kinematic pipelines prescribe a robot trajectory through geometric matching, without establishing whether it can be executed under the robot's dynamics. Prior physics-supervised neural methods train bidirectional full-sequence models on physics-refined kinematic trajectories, remaining tied to prescribed kinematic solutions and requiring noncausal context. We propose SMR, a streaming neural motion retargeter learned from semantic-conditioned physics experts. We convert human motion into robot-aware task-space targets for body landmark positions, orientations, and velocities. Physics experts track these targets directly in simulation under contact, dynamics, and actuator constraints. We train a single strictly causal Transformer on their executed state trajectories that complete the motion and pass semantic and physical validity checks. At each incoming frame, the student uses only current and past human observations to generate a robot motion reference for a downstream whole-body controller. Experiments demonstrate that semantic-conditioned physics experts generate motion with higher semantic fidelity and physical validity than direct optimization-based retargeting, while the resulting streaming retargeter achieves improved closed-loop performance over kinematic and physics-refined baselines under a common whole-body controller.

摘要（中文）：摘要：将人体运动重定向至人形机器人，需要在考虑机器人物理约束的同时保留运动语义。运动学管线通过几何匹配规定机器人轨迹，但未确定其能否在机器人动力学条件下执行。既往的物理监督神经方法在经物理精化的运动学轨迹上训练双向全序列模型，仍受限于预设的运动学解并需要非因果上下文。我们提出SMR，一种从语义条件物理专家中学习的流式神经运动重定向器。我们将人体运动转化为面向机器人任务空间的身体关键点位置、朝向及速度目标。物理专家在仿真中直接追踪这些目标，同时满足接触、动力学及执行器约束。我们基于其执行的状态轨迹训练单一严格因果Transformer，该模型完成运动并通过语义与物理有效性检验。在每个输入帧，学生模型仅利用当前及历史人体观测，为下游全身控制器生成机器人运动参考。实验表明，语义条件物理专家生成的运动在语义保真度与物理有效性上均优于基于优化的直接重定向方法，而由此得到的流式重定向器在通用全身控制器下，相较于运动学及物理精化基线，实现了更优的闭环性能。

Authors: Chun Gu, Juntong Zhang, Jingyu Li, Li Zhang

Learning to Absorb Corrections: Critic-Weighted Residual Flow for Vision-Based Insertion Manipulation

vision-based insertion residual flow policy online learning Action Chunking Transformer critic-weighted

简要说明：本文提出ACT-Flow，一种结合自适应动作分块Transformer与评论家加权残差流策略的在线学习框架，用于改善基于视觉的插入任务，在五个任务上显著优于基线。

TLDR: This paper introduces ACT-Flow, an online learning framework that combines an adaptive Action Chunking Transformer with a critic-weighted residual flow policy to improve vision-based insertion tasks, demonstrating significant success rate improvements over baselines across five tasks.

Abstract: Vision-based insertion requires correcting alignment errors while retaining useful behavior learned from demonstrations. We present ACT--Flow, an online learning framework that couples an adaptive Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) with a conditional residual flow policy. Following anchor-guided warmup, ACT absorbs successful executed actions through behavioral cloning, while residual targets are recomputed relative to the updated prior. A chunk-level critic learns from successful and failed interactions and evaluates final composed actions. Its estimates weight generated residual candidates for flow matching, complemented by supervision from successful real executions. Candidate scoring is confined to training; deployment uses RGB observations and samples one residual per action chunk. We evaluate the framework on power-plug, USB, and key insertion, together with cable routing and needle threading. Results show a five-task mean success rate of 66% at 20,000 post-initialization interaction steps, exceeding the strongest baseline by 18 percentage points at this checkpoint. Evaluations at matched checkpoints with the residual disabled show ACT's mean success increasing from 16% to 76%. Component ablations further support the complementary roles of behavior absorption, value weighting, and successful-action supervision.

摘要（中文）：基于视觉的插入操作需要在纠正对齐误差的同时，保留从示范中学习到的有效行为。我们提出了ACT--Flow，一种在线学习框架，将自适应动作分块变换器（ACT）与条件残差流策略相结合。在锚点引导的预热阶段之后，ACT通过行为克隆吸收成功执行的动作，而残差目标则相对于更新后的先验重新计算。一个分块级别的评论员从成功和失败的交互中学习，并评估最终组合成的动作。其估计值用于加权生成的残差候选，以进行流匹配，同时辅以真实成功执行的监督。候选评分仅限于训练阶段；部署时使用RGB观测，并为每个动作分块采样一个残差。我们在电源插头、USB和钥匙插入任务上评估了该框架，同时还包括线缆布线和穿针任务。结果表明，在初始化后的20,000次交互步骤中，五个任务的平均成功率为66%，在该检查点上超过最强基线18个百分点。在匹配的检查点上禁用残差进行评估时，ACT的平均成功率从16%提升至76%。组件消融实验进一步验证了行为吸收、价值加权和成功动作监督之间的互补作用。
